summary: Ambiguous SCIM-created duplicate identity causes RBAC dedup to strip all console roles, users receive 403
description:
Issue summary: Several internal employees and service accounts reported 403 Forbidden when attempting to access the internal Console and Telemetry dashboards. Impact: ~12 engineering users and 3 CI service accounts unable to access console or trigger pipelines; paging oncall and blocking runbooks. First observed ~2026-03-11 09:40 UTC.

Observed behavior: Users authenticate successfully via Okta SAML and receive a valid session cookie, but the console returns 403 with error returned from RBAC service: 'ambiguous_principal: multiple identities resolved'. Access logs show the identity-proxy submitting two distinct principal attributes for the same session (email and username alias).

Environment: Production (okta-managed SCIM + HR sync), affects Console, Telemetry Kibana, and CI pipeline triggers in us-east.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Authenticate via Okta SSO for a user with recently updated HR record. 2) Observe session token creation in identity-proxy. 3) Call Console API /api/v1/user/me -> 403 + ambiguous_principal.

Immediate impact and customer-facing risk: Internal only, but blocks oncall and release engineers.

Logs & quick evidence: - identity-proxy log (2026-03-11T09:41:12Z): "principal resolved: ['m.chen@redwood.com', 'mchen']" - rbac-service (2026-03-11T09:41:12Z): "dedup produced zero-role-set for principal group key conflict: employee_number=20482" - scim-provisioner audit (2026-03-10T03:02:00Z): "created user mchen (alias m.chen) from hr-sync batch 2026-03-10-03"
comments: Maya Chen (reporter) - 2026-03-11: Noticed multiple colleagues with the same 403 after passwordless SSO. Filed ticket and alerted #infra-support.
Ravi Patel (assignee) - 2026-03-11: Starting triage. Hypothesis: SCIM provisioning created duplicate records/aliases and RBAC dedup logic removed roles. Pulling SCIM audit logs.
SRE (Amy Wu) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed identity-proxy shows two principals against same session for affected users. Tracing shows employee_number matches between two SCIM entries.

Identity (Lars Johansson) - 2026-03-12: HR export generated duplicate user objects when a legacy alias column was present. SCIM importer created a second user with the same employee_number but different "username" attribute.
Ravi Patel - 2026-03-12: Patching RBAC dedup to prefer primary_okta_id when available; rolling patch to 10% of identity-proxy instances for mitigation.
investigation_notes: 03/11 10:05 UTC - Initial triage: Reproduced 403 in prod against affected uid mchen. Identity-proxy returns 2 principals: okta:12345 and scim:scim-67890.
03/11 11:20 UTC - SCIM audit: user m.chen and mchen created within same HR sync batch. Both entries share employee_number=20482 but different email/username casing/alias fields.

03/11 12:00 UTC - RBAC service behavior: dedup algorithm collapses principals by employee_number; on collision it currently nulls role set to avoid accidental privilege escalation. That nulling caused 0 roles -> 403.
03/12 02:10 UTC - Verified scope: 12 human users + 3 service accounts (ci-builder, infra-deploy, telemetry-scrape) affected. CI failures reported in #infra-ci with 403 when triggering jobs.

03/12 08:45 UTC - Root cause hypothesis: HR export produced duplicate user records (legacy alias column) which the SCIM importer created as separate identities. RBAC dedup is defensive but overzealous in collision cases.

03/12 09:30 UTC - Short-term mitigation tested: change dedup behavior to prefer explicit primary_okta_id or primary_email and retain role bindings if primary_okta_id present. Patch validated in staging.
03/12 10:10 UTC - Confirmed patch roll to 10% prod reduces 403 for a subset of affected users. Need full rollback/repair plan for duplicate SCIM entries and role re-assignment.
Linked artifacts: scim-provisioner logs (s3://infra-logs/scim/2026-03-10/*.gz), rbac-service traces (observability link: https://observability.redwood/services/rbac/traces?span=ambig)
resolution_notes: Mitigation (03/12): Deployed RBAC dedup patch to prefer primary_okta_id and avoid zeroing role set on employee_number collisions. Immediate effect: majority of human users regained access within 15 minutes of session refresh.

Repair (03/13): Running a targeted SCIM reconciliation job to merge duplicate entries for employee_number=20482 group and remove legacy alias-only accounts. Reconciliation job id: recon-2026-03-13-01.

Follow-up: Update SCIM importer to validate and de-duplicate HR-provided rows by employee_number before creating users. Add a preflight check in HR export job to drop legacy alias column or map it to secondary_email. Create a Confluence runbook for SCIM duplicate remediation.
Customer/Stakeholder communication: Notified Eng All and affected teams. Oncall Slack postmortem scheduled 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC.
next_steps: Complete SCIM reconciliation job and validate merged identities (owner: identity-team).
Roll RBAC dedup patch to 100% once reconciliation validated and monitor for regressions (owner: Ravi Patel).
Add unit/integration tests for importer to prevent duplicate creation (owner: scim-provisioner team).
Run postmortem and update runbook with mitigation playbook for duplicate SCIM identity events.
